Onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioner and to prove that she suffered injuries in this accident on account of rash and negligence on the part of respondent no. 1, petitioner examined herself as PW1 and tendered her affidavit Ex.PW1/A in evidence and proved the facts of her claim petition.

Petitioner as PW1 has deposed that on 28.12.2016, she and her grandmother were returning from Narela to Bahadurgarh in DTC bus bearing no. DL1PC 9789 and at abut 8.30 a.m.
they de-boarded the said DTC bus but respondent no. 1/ the driver of said DTC bus without caring for the passenger started the bus in rash and negligent manner and in a hurry.

As a result of which,
the her right leg came under the front wheel of the said DTC bus.
She suffered multiple injuries all over her body.
She was taken to R.J. Super Specialty Hospital, Bahadurgarh, for treatment.

PW1 has not at all been cross examined by the respondents no. 1 and 2 particularly by the respondent no. 1 to prove that he was not rash and negligent or that he has been falsely implicated in the present case or that accident had Tamanna Sharma Vs. Rakesh Kumar & Ors.

In her cross examination, no suggestion put to the witness with respect to manner in which the accident had occurred and she denied that accident had occurred due to her own negligence.
Nothing material has come on record to disbelieve the testimony of PW1.

Further, criminal case record Ex. PW1/1,
filed on record shows that respondent no.1 was charge sheeted by the police for offences punishable under Section 279/337/338 IPC.
Apart from deposition of PW1, the fact that petitioner suffered injuries in the accident is also supported by her medical documents MLC Ex. PW1/2 and discharge summary Ex. PW2/1.
Respondent no. 1 has not placed on record any document to disprove the factum of rash and negligent driving by him.

Further, relying upon the judgment of Mahila Dhanvanti and Ors Vs. Phulwant Mahendra Singh, Miscellaneous Appeal no.239/1992 decided by Hon'ble Madhya Pradesh High Court on 29.07.1993 in which it is held as under: -
"The plaintiff can prove the accident but cannot prove how it happened to establish negligence.

entities.text: Mahila Dhanvanti and Ors Vs. Phulwant Mahendra Singh, Miscellaneous Appeal no.239/1992
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This hardship is to be avoided by applying the principle of res ipsa loquitur.

The general purport of the words res ipsa loquitur is that the accident speaks for itself or tells its own story".
9.
Thus, Claims Tribunal while dealing with the law of torts in motor accident cases applies the principle of "res ipsa loquitur".

Considering all this, it stands proved that accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1 and petitioner suffered grievous injuries in the said accident.
Issue no. 1 is accordingly decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.

sentences.text: The learned Tribunal has taken the notional income of the deceased as Rs.22,500/- per annum i.e. Rs.1,875/- per month which is less than even the minimum wages of a daily wager.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioner suffered multiple grievous injuries all over her body.
She was taken to R.J. Super Specialty Hospital,
Bahadurgarh, for treatment.
3. Respondents no. 1 & 2 (driver & owner of the offending vehicle) in their joint written statement stated that respondent no. 1 was not driving the vehicle negligently and it is a false case against them.
Their vehicle was duly insured and they have all valid documents.
It is further alleged that the accident had occurred due to sole negligence on the part of petitioner herself.
She suffered multiple injuries all over her body.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court enhanced the earning capacity of the deceased from Rs.18,000/- to Rs.25,000/- per month".
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Respondent no. 1 has not placed on record any document to disprove the factum of rash and negligent driving by him.
Further, relying upon the judgment of Mahila Dhanvanti and Ors Vs. Phulwant Mahendra Singh, Miscellaneous Appeal no.239/1992 decided by Hon'ble Madhya Pradesh High Court on 29.07.1993 in which it is held as under: -
"The plaintiff can prove the accident but cannot prove how it happened to establish negligence.
Thus, Claims Tribunal while dealing with the law of torts in motor accident cases applies the principle of "res ipsa loquitur".
However, seeing nature of injuries suffered by petitioner, a sum of Rs. 25,000/- towards special diet and Rs. 25,000/- for conveyance awarded to the petitioner.
In Ramesh Chand Joshi v. New India Assurance Company Limited MAC. APP.
212-13/2006 decided on 20th January, 2010, the accident dated 30th July, 2004 resulted in the death of a first year student of B. Tech in Delhi College of Engineering.
Reference in this Tamanna Sharma Vs. Rakesh Kumar &
Ors.
MACT no. 233/17 Page 12 regard may be made to judgment of Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. v. Deo Pataudi, 2009 (8) Scale 194, in which case the deceased aged 22 years was a student having a brilliant career and offer of employment from a US Based Company at the time of accident.
Accordingly, the earning capacity of the petitioner is taken as Rs. 25,000/- per month as notional income and as per judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs.
Pranay Sethi and others, of Hon'ble Supreme Court petitioner is also entitled to get 40% of enhancement of salary, as petitioner is below 40 years in age.
Accordingly her functional disability is taken as 40% qua whole body.
No tax is deducted since the said income of petitioner is not taxable.
admittedly respondent no.
3 / Ins. Co. has no statutory defence.
Further, no material has come on record which shows that there is any breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy of offending vehicle.
Further, the allegations levelled in the written statement howsoever strong that may be, cannot take place of proof particularly when insurance company despite having raised the issue has not led any positive evidence on this aspect.
In view of the above and since the respondent no.3 / Ins. Co. has failed to establish any statutory defence, it is liable to indemnify the owner / insured and to pay compensation to the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.arguments: Though no evidence has placed on record, however considering the nature of injuries as the petitioner has suffered permanent disability that too above knee amputation, it is presumed that she would require attendant after the accident throughout her entire life.

This issue is therefore decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondent no.3 / Ins. Co. holding that petitioner is entitled to get compensation from respondent no.3 / Ins. Co.
